source_text:
Sententiae ad virginem
Παραίνεσις πρὸς παρθένον.
1 Ἀγάπα τὸν κύριον καὶ ἀγαπήσει σε, καὶ δούλευε αὐτῷ καὶ φωτιεῖ τὴν
καρδίαν σου.
2 Τίμα τὴν μητέρα σου ὡς μητέρα Χριστοῦ, καὶ μὴ παροξύνῃς πολιὰν
τεκούσης σε.
3 Ἀγάπα τὰς ἀδελφάς σου ὡς θυγατέρας μητρός σου, καὶ μὴ ἐγκαταλίπῃς
ὁδὸν εἰρήνης.
4 Ἀνατέλλων ὁ ἥλιος βλεπέτω τὸ βιβλίον ἐν ταῖς χερσί σου, καὶ μετὰ
δευτέραν ὥραν τὸ ἔργον σου.
5 Προσεύχου ἀδιαλείπτως, καὶ μέμνησο Χριστοῦ τοῦ γεννήσαντός σε. 6
Συντυχίας ἀνδρῶν παραιτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ γένηται εἴδωλα ἐν σῇ ψυχῇ καὶ ἔσται σοι
πρόσκομμα ἐν καιρῷ προσευχῆς. 7 Χριστὸν ἔχεις ἀγαπητόν· ἀπόρριψον ἀπό σου
ἄνδρας ἅπαντας καὶ οὐ μὴ βιώσῃς ἐπονείδιστον βίον.
8 Θυμὸν καὶ ὀργὴν μακρὰν ποίησον ἀπό σου, καὶ μνησικακία μὴ αὐλιζέσθω
ἔν σοι.
9 Μὴ εἴπῃς· σήμερον βρώσομαι καὶ αὔριον οὐ βρώσομαι, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν φρονήσει
ποιεῖς τοῦτο. ἔσται γὰρ βλάβη τῷ σώματί σου καὶ ὀδύνη τῷ στομάχῳ σου.
10 Ἐσθίειν κρέα οὐ καλὸν καὶ πίνειν οἶνον οὐκ ἀγαθόν, προσφέρειν δὲ χρὴ
ταῦτα ταῖς ἀσθενούσαις.
11 Παρθένος θρασεῖα οὐ σωθήσεται καὶ σπαταλῶσα οὐκ ὄψεται τὸν νυμφίον
αὐτῆς.
12 Μὴ εἴπῃς, ὅτι λελύπηκέ με ἡ θεραπαινὶς καὶ τίσομαι αὐτήν, διότι οὐκ ἔστιν
δουλεία ἐν θυγατράσι θεοῦ.
13 Μὴ δῷς ἀκοήν σου λόγοις ματαίοις, καὶ διηγήματα γραῶν φεῦγε
κυκλευουσῶν.
14 Ἑορτὰς μεθύσων μὴ ἴδῃς, καὶ εἰς γάμους ἀλλοτρίων μὴ εἰσέλθῃς.
ἀκάθαρτος γὰρ παρὰ κυρίῳ πᾶσα παρθένος ποιοῦσα ταῦτα.
15 Ἄνοιγε σὸν στόμα λόγῳ θεοῦ, καὶ κώλυε ἀπὸ πολυλογίας τὴν γλῶσσαν
σου.
16 Ἔναντι κυρίου ταπείνου σεαυτήν, καὶ ὑψώσει σε ἡ δεξιὰ αὐτοῦ.
17 Μὴ ἀποστρέφου πένητα ἐν καιρῷ θλίψεως, καὶ οὐ λείψει ἔλαιον ἐν τῇ
λαμπάδι σου.
thought_title: Opening counsels for a consecrated virgin
orientation: Evagrius begins his exhortation with a series of short counsels addressed directly to the virgin, urging love of Christ, honor for her mother and sisters, constant prayer, and avoidance of men, anger, luxury, and worldly distractions.
pass_a_gloss: Love the Lord and he will love you, and serve him and he will light your heart. Honor your mother as mother of Christ, and do not provoke the grey hair of the one who bore you. Love your sisters as daughters of your mother, and do not abandon the way of peace. Rising, the sun, let it see the book in your hands, and after the second hour your work. Pray without ceasing, and remember Christ who begot you. Meetings with men avoid, so that idols may not come to be in your soul and it will be to you a stumbling block in time of prayer. Christ you have as beloved; cast away from yourself all men and you will not live a reproachful life. Anger and wrath make far from you, and bearing of malice let it not lodge in you. Do not say: today I will eat and tomorrow I will not eat, because not in wisdom you do this. For there will be harm to your body and pain to your stomach. To eat meat is not good and to drink wine is not good, but it is necessary to offer these to the sick. A bold virgin will not be saved and one living luxuriously will not see her bridegroom. Do not say, that the maidservant has grieved me and I will punish her, because there is no slavery among daughters of God. Do not give your hearing to vain words, and tales of old women flee who go about. Feasts of drunkards do not see, and into weddings of strangers do not enter. For unclean before the Lord is every virgin doing these things. Open your mouth with the word of God, and restrain from much speaking your tongue. Before the Lord humble yourself, and his right hand will exalt you. Do not turn away a poor person in time of affliction, and oil will not fail in your lamp.

choices.english: the grey hair of the one who bore you
choices.why: Keeps the metonymy of grey hair as a sign of the mother's age and dignity, matching the source's concrete image rather than flattening it to 'old age.'
rejected: the old age of your mother

choices.why: The source uses the strong word for cult images; rendering it literally preserves the warning that men's images become objects of false worship in the soul.
The adjective denotes audacity and presumption; 'bold' captures the moral danger without modernizing to 'arrogant' or softening to 'forward.'
The participle describes self-indulgent, voluptuous living; the participial rendering keeps the source's characterization of a type of virgin.
The verb suggests going around from place to place, implying gossipy wandering; 'who go about' preserves the motion and the pejorative tone.
Not in this section; reserved for the following section's context.

bible_refs.note: λαμπάς, ἔλαιον, νυμφίος imagery of the ten virgins

pass_b_english: Love the Lord, and he will love you; serve him, and he will give light to your heart.
Honor your mother as the mother of Christ, and do not provoke the grey hair of the one who bore you.
Love your sisters as daughters of your mother, and do not abandon the way of peace.
When the sun rises, let it see the book in your hands, and after the second hour, your work.
Pray without ceasing, and remember Christ, who gave you birth.
Avoid meetings with men, so that idols do not arise in your soul and become a stumbling block for you at the time of prayer.
You have Christ as your beloved; cast away from yourself all men, and you will not live a shameful life.
Put anger and wrath far from you, and do not let bearing of malice lodge within you.
Do not say, "Today I will eat and tomorrow I will not eat," because you are not doing this with understanding. For it will bring harm to your body and pain to your stomach.
Eating meat is not good, and drinking wine is not good; rather, you should offer these things to those who are weak.
A bold virgin will not be saved, and one living luxuriously will not see her bridegroom.
Do not say, "The servant girl has grieved me, and I will punish her," because there is no slavery among the daughters of God.
Do not give your ear to vain words, and flee the tales of old women who go about.
Do not look upon the feasts of drunkards, and do not enter the weddings of strangers. For every virgin who does these things is unclean before the Lord.
Open your mouth with the word of God, and restrain your tongue from much speaking.
Humble yourself before the Lord, and his right hand will exalt you.
Do not turn away from the poor in time of affliction, and oil will not be lacking in your lamp.

last_rejected.quote: idols do not arise in your soul
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ γένηται εἴδωλα ἐν σῇ ψυχῇ
last_rejected.why: γένηται = 'come to be/become', not 'arise'; 'idols become' or 'idols be formed' is closer. 'Arise' suggests emergence from below, not quite right.
last_rejected.fix: so that idols do not come to be in your soul
last_rejected.ruling: γένηται = become/appear; 'arise' conveys similar sense of appearing, not a meaning change

last_rejected.why: κυκλευουσῶν means 'going around/circling', i.e., going from house to house gossiping. 'Go about' captures this. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: κυκλευουσῶν = going around/circulating; 'who go about' captures that idea

last_rejected.quote: you will not live a reproachful life.
last_rejected.why: ἐπονείδιστον means painful or tormented, not reproachful.
last_rejected.fix: you will not live a painful life.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπονείδιστον derives from ὄνειδος (reproach, disgrace); 'reproachful' is within normal semantic range.

problems.why: ἐπονείδιστον means 'shameful' or 'disgraceful' (deserving reproach), whereas English 'reproachful' means expressing disapproval toward others.
problems.ruling: ἐπονείδιστον βίον is a disgraceful, reproached life; 'reproachful' reads as blaming others, misleading the sense.

edits.old: and you will not live a reproachful life.
edits.new: and you will not live a shameful life.

fixed: mistranslation fixed: 'reproachful life' -> 'shameful life', source ἐπονείδιστον βίον means deserving reproach, not expressing it
